messages:
Asha: FYI customer Acme reported a sharp p99 latency spike on their dedicated pool at ~02:28 UTC, app-level timeouts and some 500s. They attach traces showing GPU stall before the slowdown.
Devin: Can you paste the trace + tenant id? suspect KV cache growth or fragmentation.
Asha: Paste: tenant=acme-42, traces: https://redwood/logs/trace/abcd1234, sample: long tail of token gen, GPU memory creeping before p99 jump. No OOMs in syslog but observed slow GC.
Marco: ops-bot, can you pull pod metrics for the affected host (node gpu-12) and nvidia-smi output for the timeframe?
ops-bot: pulled metrics: node=gpu-12, window=02:00-03:00 UTC. GPU mem used climbs from 5.6GB -> 11.9GB over ~30m, p99 latency from 220ms -> 1.6s. No CUDA OOMs recorded, but kernel preemption high. logs: /var/log/infer-runtime/instance-4721.log snippet attached.
Devin: that pattern looks like KV growth with fragmentation. If KV cache keeps growing past slab thresholds we see increased compaction stalls. Any inferctl dump-kv for that tenant?
Asha: running dump now, output shows KV entries ballooned to ~1.4M keys for tenant acme-42, avg value size 1.6KB.
Marco: ouch. That many small KV items will fragment GPU allocator. We should: 1) cap per-tenant KV entries, 2) trigger compact on large tenants, 3) throttle tail latency by backpressure. Immediate mitigation: can we evict tenant from the hot GPU and re-route to spare?
Devin: yes, we have a soft-evict flow. Asha, can you run the evict command:
```
# move tenant to spare pool
infractl tenant-evict --tenant acme-42 --target spare-pool-2 --reason "kv-bloat p99 mitigation"
```
Asha: running now... confirmed migration started at 02:36 UTC.
ops-bot: migration completed for worker 4721 -> spare-pool-2 at 02:39 UTC.
Asha: p95/p99 dropped back to baseline within ~3m post-migration: p99 1.6s -> 210ms. Customer confirmed reduced errors. :thumbsup:
Devin: good. Root cause analysis next: why did KV grow? Need repro steps and safe defaults. I suspect: customer prompt pattern with heavy context windows and no prefix caching TTL. Also GC thresholds were conservative.
Marco: on the node we saw allocator slab utilization uneven: many small allocations causing internal fragmentation. Suggestions: bump compaction aggressiveness and add periodic slab defrag task. Also add a per-tenant KV-entry cap and an eviction LRU with bounded memory.
Devin: propose sequence of changes: 1) immediate prod patch: lower KV soft_limit to 800k entries per tenant and enable aggressive compaction flag (runtime.conf: kv.compact_aggressive=true), 2) rollout a memory allocator tune to reduce fragment threshold from 0.25 -> 0.15, 3) add telemetry to alert on sustained KV growth > 10k/min for 10m.
Asha: can we do canary patch on spare-pool-2 first?
Devin: yes, will push canary at 03:20 UTC. Patch details:
```
# runtime.conf snippet
kv.soft_limit_entries=800000
kv.compact_aggressive=true
allocator.fragment_threshold=0.15
```
We'll also add an auto-evict policy if tenant KV growth > 50% week-over-week.
Marco: capturing logs and heap profiles for affected period; please collect the following from the node for postmortem:
```
kubectl -n infer logs -l app=infer-runtime --since=2h | gzip -c > /tmp/infer-logs-4721.gz
inferctl heap-profile --node gpu-12 --out /tmp/heap-4721.pb
inferctl kv-stats --tenant acme-42 --since 03:00
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 60 --filename /tmp/gpu-sample.csv
```
Devin: also capture per-tenant request distribution and sequence length histogram; if they sent lots of long context calls we need to recommend prompt-window limits.
Asha: noted. I'll open a support follow-up to Acme advising best practices (context window limits, streaming chunking, TTL on conversation state).
ops-bot: can confirm canary rollout succeeded, KV soft_limit enforced on canary, no regressions after 45m.
Devin: plan for next steps: backlog ticket for allocator defrag task, telemetry alert, and a code change to cap per-tenant KV entries with LRU eviction. Assigning to eng-runtime.
Marco: schedule postmortem and customer RCA doc. Asha, please coordinate customer comms and link the mitigation timeline.
Asha: will do. thanks team.
Devin: one last note — add a lightweight mitigation doc to run in oncall: steps to detect KV bloat and trigger tenant-evict + canary patch commands. Keep it <1 page.
Asha: creating that runbook now and will ping #oncall when ready.
